record.paper_title: Formal languages and arithmetic theories: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Let p be an integer at least 2 and let Sigma = {0, ..., p - 1}. A deterministic finite automaton over synchronized p-ary encodings can recognize arithmetic predicates such as addition, where an addition automaton over Sigma^3 accepts exactly triples of p-ary encodings of natural numbers x, y, z with x + y = z. Is there a syntactically defined subclass A of deterministic finite automata that contains these addition-predicate automata and has the following polynomial-witness property: for every finite family A1, ..., Am of automata in A, if the intersection L(A1) ∩ ... ∩ L(Am) is nonempty, must that intersection contain some word whose length is bounded by a polynomial in |A1| + ... + |Am|?

evidence.quote: This observation gives rise to the following open problem.

Open Problem 1. Is there a syntactic subclass A of DFA that includes the DFA for the addition predicate such that for any A1, . . . , Am ∈ A, if their intersection L = Tm i=1 L(Ai) is non-empty then L contains a word of length polynomial in |A1| + · · · + |Am|?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer p ≥ 2 and let Σ = {0, 1, …, p−1}. For a natural number n, write its base-p digits (least or most significant first, fixed by convention) and pad with leading zeros so that several encodings can be aligned to a common length. A k-tuple (n_1, …, n_k) of natural numbers is then encoded as a word over Σ^k by reading the aligned digits coordinatewise. The addition predicate is the language A_+ ⊆ (Σ^3)* consisting of all synchronized base-p encodings of triples (x, y, z) of natural numbers satisfying x + y = z; it is recognized by a deterministic finite automaton (DFA), called the addition automaton.

Question: Does there exist a syntactically defined subclass 𝒜 of DFAs such that

(i) 𝒜 contains the addition automaton (over base-p alphabets, for every p ≥ 2), and

(ii) 𝒜 has the following polynomial-witness property: there is a polynomial P such that for every finite family A_1, …, A_m of automata in 𝒜, whenever the intersection L(A_1) ∩ ⋯ ∩ L(A_m) is nonempty it contains a word of length at most P(|A_1| + ⋯ + |A_m|), where |A_i| denotes the size (number of states) of A_i?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of identifying a syntactic DFA subclass containing the addition automaton with polynomial-length witnesses for non-empty intersections is posed as an open problem. Related results show polynomial-witness bounds exist for certain restricted classes (e.g., level 3/2 of the Straubing–Thérien hierarchy via partially ordered NFAs), but no such class encompassing addition automata is currently known. General DFA intersection non-emptiness is PSPACE-complete and lacks polynomial-length witnesses unless complexity classes collapse.

status_evidence.title: On the Complexity of Intersection Non-emptiness for Star-Free Language Classes
status_evidence.snippet: For languages at level 3/2 of the Straubing–Thérien hierarchy, the minimum length of a word in the intersection is polynomially bounded in the sizes of partially ordered NFAs accepting them.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial-witness bounds are known only for certain restricted syntactic subclasses, not in a class containing addition automata.

status_evidence.title: Finite Automata Intersection Non-Emptiness
status_evidence.snippet: DFA intersection non-emptiness is PSPACE-complete in general.
status_evidence.claim: In the unrestricted DFA setting polynomial witnesses are not expected, motivating the search for a suitable syntactic subclass.
